neighbours.label: a verb of stopping or exiting an ongoing activity (end, stop, leave, quit, abort, break off), on the verb
fire: If the server does not answer, the script should abort and log the error.
After the third warning, the referee decided to stop the match.
When the music gets boring, we usually just quit and go home.
Once the battery runs low, the recording will stop on its own.
If the talks fail again, the union may walk out of the meeting.
At midnight the party had to end because of the neighbours.
When nobody is listening, the speaker should simply give up.
If the loop finds a match, the program will break and return it.
quiet: If the server does not answer, the script should retry and log the error.
After the third warning, the referee decided to continue the match.
When the music gets boring, we usually just dance and stay late.
Once the battery runs low, the recording will slow on its own.
If the talks fail again, the union may ask for another meeting.
At midnight the party had to move because of the neighbours.
When nobody is listening, the speaker should simply speak louder.
If the loop finds a match, the program will save and print it.

notes: Card peaks: ' up' x7 (give up), ' stop' x3, ' break', ' end', ' leave', ' abort', Russian 'встал'. Probe: 'the game will end' 0.84 vs 'continue' 0.18; 'always leave' 0.29 vs 'stay' 0.01. The other side of the distinction is continuing/staying; near misses use those verbs.
